summary.oneLiner: Northern Arc closed FY26 with its highest-ever quarterly profit (₹133cr, +251% YoY, +32% QoQ) on AUM of ₹16,594cr (+22% YoY, +10% QoQ), led by the direct-to-customer (D2C) book now at 59% of AUM (vs 19% in FY21) — a mix shift management credits for ~380bps of five-year NIM expansion (5.6%→9.4%); asset quality and credit cost improved steadily through the year (FY26 credit cost 2.8% vs 3.2% in FY25), helped in part by a February-2026 RBI guideline permitting FLDG cash-collateral to be netted against ECL, which management is explicit was a genuine but partly optical/regulatory-driven, not credit-quality-driven, improvement. Guidance for FY27: 22-25% AUM growth, ROA of 3%+ near-term, and mid-to-high-teens ROE (15-17%) over the next 8-10 quarters.

> **One-offs / adjustments called out explicitly:** In Feb-2026 RBI issued guidelines allowing NBFCs to net cash-collateral FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) against ECL provisioning — this reduced the Stage-2 ECL coverage from ~24% (Dec-25) to ~12% (Mar-26), which management stressed is a regulatory/optical shift, not a credit-quality change (the underlying loss exposure was always covered by partner FLDG). As a "prudent measure," the company simultaneously created a ₹66cr management overlay against unforeseen macro risk (West Asia geopolitical tension). Under direct analyst questioning (Pavan Kumar), CFO/Risk head confirmed that if the FY25 one-time ₹68cr DLG-related provision (of an ₹80cr requirement) is normalized against the FY26 Q4 write-back (only ₹29cr, Q4-only not full-year), the "clean" Q4 credit cost would have been closer to ₹120cr (~2.9-3.0%) rather than the reported (lower) figure — i.e. steady-state credit cost is guided at 2.7-2.8%, not the optically-lower printed number. CFO confirmed: "It's pure organic, except for the DLG... there is no one-off" on Aviom (legacy exposure still provided for, no write-back there).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **AUM/loan growth (FY27):** "three times of GDP" → 22-25%, explicit Street commitment; company has "recalibrated some segments/sectors" to stay prudent on risk.
- **ROA:** near-term target 3%+ (FY26 exited at 2.8% full-year, Q4 already at 3.3%).
- **ROE:** mid-to-high-teens over "8 to 10 quarters" — specifically clarified as **15% to 17%** (not 15-18% as one analyst initially framed it).
- **Credit cost:** steady-state guidance **2.7% to 2.8%**, net of FLDG benefit and the ₹66cr overlay.
- **D2C mix:** targeted to rise from 59% to **65%** of AUM — management flagged this as the key driver of further NIM expansion.
- **Cost of funds:** guided to hold at **8.5-8.6%** (not expected to fall further as rates are seen "bottoming out"); yield improvement from D2C mix shift expected to offset, not a cost-of-fund tailwind.
- **Rural/MFI book:** being rebuilt cautiously from a trough of ~₹900cr (deliberately cut from ~₹1,500cr in late-2024) — "building it back" given improved collection-efficiency evidence, but no explicit AUM growth number given for FY27.
- **Affordable housing:** board-approved product, to be launched only once the LAP book "reaches a certain size and scale" — no FY27 launch commitment.
order book & pipeline:
Not applicable in the traditional order-book sense (financial lender); pipeline equivalents by segment:
- **Consumer Finance:** AUM ₹5,000cr+ (D2C); ~25,000-26,000 loans/day underwritten; targeted risk-adjusted yield 15-16%; 70% repeat-customer rate.
- **MSME Finance:** AUM ₹3,691cr, +43% YoY; 17 new branches added in FY26; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.4% (Mar-26, up from 97.8% Sep-25); average ticket size ₹11-15 lakh; yield 17-18% (explicitly "not chasing 24%").
- **Rural Finance (MFI):** AUM ₹1,009cr, +8% QoQ; highest-ever quarterly disbursement ₹305cr (+17% QoQ); 64 branches added in Q4 → 342-branch network; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.6% (Mar-26); Karnataka-ordinance-impacted collection efficiency recovered from 94.5% to ~99.5%.
- **Credit Solutions (fee-based):** 368 originating partners (90% rated BBB and above; ~95% with capital adequacy >20%); FY26 placement volume ₹11,834cr (placement fee income ₹31cr, +22% YoY); credit funds AUM ₹3,092cr (fee income ₹38cr in FY26); ~₹10,000cr of securitization placed in FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Consumer Finance:** partner-distributed digital/merchant lending; ~28 partners referenced by an analyst; risk-adjusted yield held at 15-16% band by design (deliberately reduced short-tenure book to near-zero, capped end-APR); ROA on this vertical "upward of close to about 4%" per CEO — materially higher than blended company ROA.
- **MSME Finance:** secured LAP-style lending (100% registered mortgage), branch-network-led; recalibrated to avoid overlap with MFI-graduate segments; addressable credit gap in MSME estimated at ~24% (~₹30 lakh crore industry-wide) — framed as long runway.
- **Rural Finance/MFI:** 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU; 100% underwritten via proprietary "Nu Score" scorecard; full-year credit cost improved from 6.7% to 4.9% in FY26; GNPA "negligible" at ~4bps.
- **Credit Solutions:** capital-light fee engine complementing balance-sheet lending — placements, credit funds (new funds being launched), a bonds platform, and securitization (PTC transactions) all cited as growth levers for FY27.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Affordable housing (board-approved, gated on LAP book maturity).
- Expanded consumer-finance financing-solution partnerships ("convenient financing solution" embedded with partners).
- New credit funds being launched under the Credit Solutions platform; bonds platform build-out.
- Continued branch expansion in MSME (physical footprint + productivity) and rural (342 branches and growing).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Underwriting data/AI stack:** 50 million+ data points, 30+ underwriting models across businesses, explicitly cited as a competitive edge (management repeatedly ties this to risk-adjusted-yield discipline).
- **Risk-team scale + ground coverage:** 100+ dedicated risk professionals; on-ground visits to ~1/3 of the ~680 districts where the company/partners operate (~220 districts covered in granular detail) — cited as giving "far more granular touch and feel" than peers.
- **Conservative provisioning policy:** 100% provision on 90+ DPD unsecured loans — management argues this is a near-term-credit-cost headwind vs. peers but structurally reduces carried-forward delinquent pool.
- **Partner-quality moat in Credit Solutions:** 90% of the 368 originating partners rated BBB+ and ~95% with capital adequacy >20% — evidenced, not just asserted.
- **Placement/securitization franchise:** ~₹10,000cr of securitization placed in FY26 — cited by CEO as a structural competitive moat alongside the fee-income platform.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM 9.4% in FY26 (+25bps YoY per CFO's Q4 framing; the CEO's opening remarks frame a longer 5-year, +380bps move from 5.6% in FY21, driven by D2C mix rising from 19% to 59%).
- Cost of funds: FY26 8.5% (-48bps YoY); incremental cost of funds Q4FY26 ~8.6-8.7% (down from 9.3% a year ago).
- Funding mix shift: fixed-rate share of borrowings rose from ~30% to ~40% as management called the rate-cut cycle "bottoming out"; bank-borrowing share deliberately reduced from ~65% (Mar-25) to ~52% (Mar-26) in favor of offshore/DFI (25% of funding) and capital-market issuances (NCDs, ECBs) — a diversification choice flagged by one analyst as counter-intuitive given rising market yields.
- Opex ratio flat YoY: FY26 3.6%, Q4FY26 3.7%.
- Management explicitly does **not** expect further cost-of-fund reduction from the current 8.5-8.6% level; NIM expansion for FY27 is expected to come from D2C mix (59%→65%), not funding-cost tailwinds. CFO flagged a risk of RBI rate hikes given rising inflation, with limited transmission from banks even after prior repo cuts.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Branch network: 66 branches added (2 merged) company-wide in the quarter; MSME added 17 new branches in FY26; Rural added 64 branches in Q4 alone, taking the rural network to 342 branches (after a prior period of deliberate contraction).
- No physical-capex/commissioning items (financial-services business); expansion is branch/distribution-led and calibrated to collection-efficiency evidence (rural AUM being rebuilt only after collection efficiency proof points, not ahead of it).
capital allocation:
- Tangible net worth ₹3,896cr, +13% YoY; debt-equity improved from 3.9x (Mar-24) to 3.1x (Mar-26).
- Capital adequacy 22.6%, "well above regulatory requirement," management flags this as headroom to grow the balance sheet over the "next two to three years" without fresh capital raise being signaled on this call.
- Liquidity surplus ~₹1,250cr (cash/bank balance + undrawn bank sanctions) as of 31-Mar-26, with positive cumulative mismatch across all time buckets.
- Total borrowings ₹12,258cr per CFO's prepared remarks (later referenced as ~₹12,900cr by the CEO in Q&A — flagged here as a discrepancy in the transcript, not reconciled on the call); ~60% linked to variable interest rates.
risks & watch-items:
- **West Asia geopolitical tension:** flagged repeatedly as a live risk; drove the ₹66cr prudential overlay; MSME exposure to gas/petrol/chemicals/pesticide sectors kept deliberately under 2% of book, and underwriting recalibrated from Feb-2026 onward in response.
- **Stage-2/Stage-3 ECL-coverage optics:** an analyst (Raghav) directly challenged why ECL coverage is now lower than even FY24 levels; management's answer (FLDG-portfolio-mix shift + Stage-3 mix shifting toward secured MSME) is plausible but is a genuine area to re-verify next quarter given it is a regulatory-interpretation-driven change rather than a portfolio-de-risking one.
- **Rate environment:** CFO expects rates have "bottomed out" and flagged possible RBI hikes on rising inflation — a cost-of-funds risk to the NIM-expansion thesis if it materializes faster than the D2C-mix offset.
- **MSME competitive intensity:** management explicitly recalibrated MSME/merchant-lending strategy citing overlap with MFI-graduate segments and rising participant count in some sub-segments.
- **Segment-level disclosure granularity reduced:** an analyst (Pavan Kumar) noted quarterly (vs. only full-year) credit-cost-by-segment disclosure was missing from this quarter's presentation — management acknowledged and said it would be provided ("it will be in the full-year basis" currently).
management quality / tone: Confident and detailed; CEO gave explicit, numbers-backed FY27 guidance (22-25% AUM growth, 3%+ ROA, 15-17% ROE in 8-10 quarters) rather than vague directional commentary. When pressed hard by two analysts (Raghav, Pavan Kumar) on the ECL-coverage decline and the FLDG-driven credit-cost optics, management (CEO + Risk Head) walked through the reconciliation math transparently, including conceding what the "clean" like-for-like credit cost would have been (~₹120cr/2.9-3.0% for Q4) rather than letting the lower reported number stand unchallenged. Also responsive to a direct disclosure-granularity ask (segment-level quarterly credit cost) with a commitment to reinstate it.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The FY26 credit-cost improvement (3.2%→2.8%) is **partly a regulatory-interpretation change** (Feb-2026 RBI FLDG/ECL netting guideline), not purely an asset-quality improvement — Stage-2 ECL coverage fell from ~24% to ~12% QoQ for this reason, and management's own math implies a "clean" Q4 credit cost of ~₹120cr vs. the lower reported figure.
- Stage-3 asset composition has structurally shifted toward **secured MSME (collateral-backed)** because unsecured retail loans are written off at 90 DPD under company policy — this mechanically lowers blended ECL-coverage ratios without implying a change in overall book risk.
- Consumer Finance ROA ("upward of ~4%") is disclosed as materially above the blended company ROA (2.8-3.3%), making it the highest-return-on-assets segment even though its risk-adjusted yield (15-16%) is not the headline-highest yield in the book.
- Bank-borrowing dependency was **deliberately cut** from 65% to 52% of the funding mix even as market yields rose — a proactive diversification decision (more offshore/DFI + capital-market issuances), not a signal of bank-side funding stress.
- Rural/MFI AUM is being rebuilt only in lockstep with collection-efficiency proof points (99.6% X-bucket in March), after having been deliberately shrunk by ~40% (₹1,500cr→₹900cr) through the prior stress cycle — a calibrated re-entry, not a return to pre-cycle risk appetite.

- Management explicitly does **not** expect further cost-of-fund reduction from the current 8.5-8.6% level; NIM expansion for FY27 is expected to come from D2C mix (59%→65%), not funding-cost tailwinds. CFO flagged a risk of RBI rate hikes given rising inflation, with limited transmission from banks even after prior repo cuts.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Branch network: 66 branches added (2 merged) company-wide in the quarter; MSME added 17 new branches in FY26; Rural added 64 branches in Q4 alone, taking the rural network to 342 branches (after a prior period of deliberate contraction).
- No physical-capex/commissioning items (financial-services business); expansion is branch/distribution-led and calibrated to collection-efficiency evidence (rural AUM being rebuilt only after collection efficiency proof points, not ahead of it).
capital allocation:
- Tangible net worth ₹3,896cr, +13% YoY; debt-equity improved from 3.9x (Mar-24) to 3.1x (Mar-26).
- Capital adequacy 22.6%, "well above regulatory requirement," management flags this as headroom to grow the balance sheet over the "next two to three years" without fresh capital raise being signaled on this call.
- Liquidity surplus ~₹1,250cr (cash/bank balance + undrawn bank sanctions) as of 31-Mar-26, with positive cumulative mismatch across all time buckets.
- Total borrowings ₹12,258cr per CFO's prepared remarks (later referenced as ~₹12,900cr by the CEO in Q&A — flagged here as a discrepancy in the transcript, not reconciled on the call); ~60% linked to variable interest rates.

- **West Asia geopolitical tension:** flagged repeatedly as a live risk; drove the ₹66cr prudential overlay; MSME exposure to gas/petrol/chemicals/pesticide sectors kept deliberately under 2% of book, and underwriting recalibrated from Feb-2026 onward in response.
- **Stage-2/Stage-3 ECL-coverage optics:** an analyst (Raghav) directly challenged why ECL coverage is now lower than even FY24 levels; management's answer (FLDG-portfolio-mix shift + Stage-3 mix shifting toward secured MSME) is plausible but is a genuine area to re-verify next quarter given it is a regulatory-interpretation-driven change rather than a portfolio-de-risking one.

- **MSME competitive intensity:** management explicitly recalibrated MSME/merchant-lending strategy citing overlap with MFI-graduate segments and rising participant count in some sub-segments.
- **Segment-level disclosure granularity reduced:** an analyst (Pavan Kumar) noted quarterly (vs. only full-year) credit-cost-by-segment disclosure was missing from this quarter's presentation — management acknowledged and said it would be provided ("it will be in the full-year basis" currently).
management quality / tone: Confident and detailed; CEO gave explicit, numbers-backed FY27 guidance (22-25% AUM growth, 3%+ ROA, 15-17% ROE in 8-10 quarters) rather than vague directional commentary. When pressed hard by two analysts (Raghav, Pavan Kumar) on the ECL-coverage decline and the FLDG-driven credit-cost optics, management (CEO + Risk Head) walked through the reconciliation math transparently, including conceding what the "clean" like-for-like credit cost would have been (~₹120cr/2.9-3.0% for Q4) rather than letting the lower reported number stand unchallenged. non-obvious takeaways:

- Consumer Finance ROA ("upward of ~4%") is disclosed as materially above the blended company ROA (2.8-3.3%), making it the highest-return-on-assets segment even though its risk-adjusted yield (15-16%) is not the headline-highest yield in the book.

- Rural/MFI AUM is being rebuilt only in lockstep with collection-efficiency proof points (99.6% X-bucket in March), after having been deliberately shrunk by ~40% (₹1,500cr→₹900cr) through the prior stress cycle — a calibrated re-entry, not a return to pre-cycle risk appetite.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Business model spans three legs across MSME, Consumer and Rural sectors: Direct to Customer Lending (AUM INR 10,766 Cr), Credit Solutions Lending (AUM INR 6,089 Cr), plus Fund Management (AUM INR 2,988 Cr), Placements (volumes INR 1,611 Cr) and Tech Solutions.
- Rated AA-(Stable) by ICRA Limited & India Ratings; the deck frames the AUM and profit record as "Demonstrating growth in AUM and profitability across business cycles", tagging Demonetization, IL&FS Crisis, Covid Pandemic and MFI overleverage stress on the chart.
- Credit Solutions is described as "Powering Originator Partners Across the Full Credit Continuum" with 373 Originator Partners, 1,500+ Investor Partners, 15 years of track record on Lending and 10 years on Placement, and a claim of being a "Dominant player in securitization/PTC" with "Credit placement of Rs. 1.3 lakh Cr till date" and "Zero credit risk" on the placement business.
- Marquee shareholder base (as on June 30, 2026) includes LeapFrog Financial Inclusion India (II), Accion Africa-Asia, Eight Roads Investments Mauritius II, Ashish Dhawan & Group, Augusta Investments II, International Finance Corporation and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, described as "Marquee Investors Driving Strong Corporate Governance Standards".

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Consumer Finance:** partner-distributed digital/merchant lending; ~28 partners referenced by an analyst; risk-adjusted yield held at 15-16% band by design (deliberately reduced short-tenure book to near-zero, capped end-APR); ROA on this vertical "upward of close to about 4%" per CEO — materially higher than blended company ROA.
- **MSME Finance:** secured LAP-style lending (100% registered mortgage), branch-network-led; recalibrated to avoid overlap with MFI-graduate segments; addressable credit gap in MSME estimated at ~24% (~₹30 lakh crore industry-wide) — framed as long runway.
- **Rural Finance/MFI:** 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU; 100% underwritten via proprietary "Nu Score" scorecard; full-year credit cost improved from 6.7% to 4.9% in FY26; GNPA "negligible" at ~4bps.
- **Credit Solutions:** capital-light fee engine complementing balance-sheet lending — placements, credit funds (new funds being launched), a bonds platform, and securitization (PTC transactions) all cited as growth levers for FY27.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
Not applicable in the traditional order-book sense (financial lender); pipeline equivalents by segment:

- **Rural Finance (MFI):** AUM ₹1,009cr, +8% QoQ; highest-ever quarterly disbursement ₹305cr (+17% QoQ); 64 branches added in Q4 → 342-branch network; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.6% (Mar-26); Karnataka-ordinance-impacted collection efficiency recovered from 94.5% to ~99.5%.
- **Credit Solutions (fee-based):** 368 originating partners (90% rated BBB and above; ~95% with capital adequacy >20%); FY26 placement volume ₹11,834cr (placement fee income ₹31cr, +22% YoY); credit funds AUM ₹3,092cr (fee income ₹38cr in FY26); ~₹10,000cr of securitization placed in FY26.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **AUM/loan growth (FY27):** "three times of GDP" → 22-25%, explicit Street commitment; company has "recalibrated some segments/sectors" to stay prudent on risk.
- **ROA:** near-term target 3%+ (FY26 exited at 2.8% full-year, Q4 already at 3.3%).
- **ROE:** mid-to-high-teens over "8 to 10 quarters" — specifically clarified as **15% to 17%** (not 15-18% as one analyst initially framed it).
- **Credit cost:** steady-state guidance **2.7% to 2.8%**, net of FLDG benefit and the ₹66cr overlay.
- **D2C mix:** targeted to rise from 59% to **65%** of AUM — management flagged this as the key driver of further NIM expansion.
- **Cost of funds:** guided to hold at **8.5-8.6%** (not expected to fall further as rates are seen "bottoming out"); yield improvement from D2C mix shift expected to offset, not a cost-of-fund tailwind.
- **Rural/MFI book:** being rebuilt cautiously from a trough of ~₹900cr (deliberately cut from ~₹1,500cr in late-2024) — "building it back" given improved collection-efficiency evidence, but no explicit AUM growth number given for FY27.
- **Affordable housing:** board-approved product, to be launched only once the LAP book "reaches a certain size and scale" — no FY27 launch commitment.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Label conflict] The Q1FY27 highlights slide labels INR 16,855 Cr as "Lending AUM", while the AUM trend slide and the sector asset-quality table call the same INR 16,855 Cr figure "Total AUM" / "Overall AUM". Both readings are quoted as printed.
- [Internal inconsistency] Business-overview slides state 430 branches, 30 active digital partners and 373 Originator Partners, whereas the ICRA ESG write-up cites 432 branches, 57 digital partners and 368 Originator Partners. Similarly Credit Solutions states "Loan to Originate — AUM of Rs. 6,104 Cr" while the IR Lending slide shows Lending AUM of 6,089 (Jun-26).
- [Placements] Placement volumes are explicitly described as "subdued in midst of geopolitical tension", at INR 1,611 Cr; Gross Transaction Volume disbursements were 4,430 (Q1FY26) versus 4,221 (Q1FY27).
- [Prior-year provision] The PAT chart carries the note "FY25 includes one time provision of INR 68 crore on account of DLG provision".
- [Originator quality] Of Originator Partners, 88% are BBB & above rated and 95% have CRAR of 20%+; lending is secured by "110%-120% collateral of retail loans".
